summary: Cauchy–Schwarz for the integral of β_c(y)β_c'(γ⁻¹y)‖W(y)‖‖W(γ⁻¹y)‖, splitting the integrand as √(f·g) with the Schur weights; the frame-volume factors of the two weights cancel.

steps.claim: Write the second Schur integral first and substitute y ↦ γ_∞⁻¹·y in it (left invariance of Haar measure on G_∞), so that both Schur integrals are integrals in the same variable y.

Apply Cauchy–Schwarz (sq_lintegral_le): it suffices to show, at each y, h(y)² ≤ f(y)·g(y) for the integrand h of amplitudeAbs and the integrands f, g of the two Schur integrals; the measurability conditions hold.
Suppose the pointwise inequality fails at some y; then h(y) ≠ 0, so β_c(y), β_c'(γ_∞⁻¹y) and the Bessel kernel at (γ, y) are nonzero.
steps.lean: by_contra! ⟨_, n⟩; cases by simpa using n.ne_zero

steps.claim: Then both y and γ_∞⁻¹y are InCut (the kernel is nonzero) and, by the box-partition property of the chosen weights, both lie in the boxes, so the box cutoffs equal the class cutoffs; with ‖K(γ,y)‖ = ∏_v‖W_v(y_v)‖·∏_v‖W_v((γ_∞⁻¹y)_v)‖ the failing inequality reads β_c β_c' ‖W(y)‖²‖W(γ⁻¹y)‖² > β_cβ_c'‖W(y)‖²‖W(γ⁻¹y)‖²·∏_v(Δ(y_v)/Δ((γ⁻¹y)_v))^{k+n}·∏_v(Δ((γ⁻¹y)_v)/Δ(y_v))^{k+n}.
steps.lean:
simp_all [boxCutoff, classCutoff, boxedPoints, ↓inCut_of_besselKernel_ne_zero ‹_›,
    (isBoxPartition_epsilon c).2, ↓(isBoxPartition_epsilon c').2, enorm_besselKernel, schurWeight,
    sq]; ac_nf at n

steps.claim: The product of the two frame-volume factors is 1 (Δ > 0), so the failing inequality is x > x, a contradiction.
steps.lean:
simp [← mul_assoc, ← prod_mul_distrib, ← ofReal_mul, ← mul_pow, field,
    frameVolume_pos, le_of_lt, ne_of_gt] at n
